edition.locus: Gebhardt III.VI (the customary place; secret burial; amen)

source_text: Οἱ ἅγιοι μάρτυρες δοξάσαντες τὸν θεόν, ἐξελθόντες ἐπὶ τὸν συνήθη τόπον ἀπετμήθησαν τὰς κεφαλάς, καὶ ἐτελείωσαν αὐτῶν τὴν μαρτυρίαν ἐν τῇ τοῦ σωτῆρος ὁμολογίᾳ. Τινὲς δὲ τῶν πιστῶν λαθραίως αὐτῶν τὰ σώματα λαβόντες κατέθεντο ἐν τόπῳ ἐπιτηδείῳ, συνεργασάσης αὐτοῖς τῆς χάριτος τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ· ᾧ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, ἀμήν.
pass_a_gloss: The holy martyrs, having glorified God and having gone out to the customary place, were cut off as to their heads, and they finished their testimony in the confession of the Savior. But some of the believers, having secretly taken their bodies, deposited them in a suitable place, the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ having worked together with them, to whom be the glory unto the ages of the ages, amen.
pass_b_english: After giving glory to God, the holy martyrs went out to the accustomed place and were beheaded, and they brought their witness to its fulfillment by confessing the Savior.
Then some of the believers took their bodies in secret and laid them in a fitting place, with the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ assisting them, to whom be glory for ever and ever, amen.

lemmas.gloss: holy ones set apart for God

choices.why: aorist passive verb with accusative of respect for the body part, so rendered as a single English passive for natural reading
rejected: were cut off as to the heads

choices.english: brought their witness to its fulfillment
choices.why: aorist active with direct object denotes completing the course of testimony by death, not merely ending speech
